messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition follows the rule a + b = round(a + b), where the exact sum is rounded to the nearest representable value in a finite mantissa. Because each rounding discards some low‑order bits, the intermediate result of (a + b) can differ from the exact sum, so when we then add c the final rounding may produce a different value than computing a + (b + c) where the rounding occurs after the second addition instead. Consequently, the limited precision and successive rounding operations break the mathematical associativity property for floating‑point addition.
